subject: gov.policy
name: Cotonou cyber-hub programme
position_end: Incubator, statewide EBIOS framework, crisis exercise and 300 unit heads trained
note: host of the Cyber Africa Forum, a cybersecurity-only incubator, a statewide EBIOS Risk Manager framework, a crisis exercise for state information-security officers and 300 police unit heads trained in 2026

subject: gov.policy
name: Déclaration de politique sectorielle: Orientations stratégiques 2021
position_end: The 2016-2021 digital-economy sector strategy, with six flagship projects and six structural reforms and the aim of making the country West Africa's digital services platform; its term ended in 2021

subject: gov.policy
name: Machinery of government for digital
position_end: Renamed Transformation Digitale et Innovation with an AI-strategy mandate, its remit and organisation fixed by decree 2026-396; budget codes moved
note: the April 2026 poll returned a new government; on 27 May the digital portfolio changed hands and the ministry was renamed Transformation Digitale et Innovation with an explicit national AI-strategy mandate, and décret 2026-314 moved the budget programme codes so any Benin budget series keyed on ministry breaks at 2026-05-24

subject: gov.policy
name: Mandatory digitisation of paper records
position_end: Every state structure required to move archives onto digital tools; no deadline, budget or compliance mechanism
note: a joint circular requires every state structure to move archive and procedure management onto digital tools, with returns stated as fiscal and environmental rather than as service improvement; no implementation deadline, budget line, scope definition or compliance mechanism is stated

subject: gov.policy
name: National broadband infrastructure programme
position_end: The programme stands as the broadband instrument; no separate broadband strategy document is adopted

subject: gov.policy
name: National Digital Committee
position_end: Attached to the presidency and chaired by the head of state, meeting quarterly; it steers digital transformation, tracks digital projects through a permanent secretariat's quarterly dashboard and gives a prior opinion on structuring projects and on technology partnerships that could engage digital sovereignty

subject: gov.policy
name: National DPI roadmap
position_end: In draft on a once-only principle; the agency frames the hard part as governance
note: drafted with the Digital Impact Alliance and the Centre for Digital Public Infrastructure to link fragmented government systems around a once-only principle — the state ceasing to ask citizens for documents it issued itself; the agency frames the hard part as governance and coherence across infrastructure already built

subject: gov.policy
name: Presidential programme 2026-2033 digital commitments
position_end: Commits to a data-localisation law, supercomputers and a data-monetising platform
note: commits to a data-localisation law, national supercomputers and a state platform monetising locally produced data, and counts a government AI super app among its existing foundations; nothing held establishes that the super app exists

subject: gov.policy
name: Single-agency identity governance
milestone: One presidency-attached agency owns all four registers
position_end: Identity, population, civil and electoral registers under one agency
note: one presidency-attached agency is responsible for identity, the population register and the electoral register, and its director general doubles as National Civil Registrar; framed by the agency as a structural decision rather than a technical one

subject: gov.policy
name: Stratégie numérique 2031
position_end: In drafting with external facilitation
sources: 2026-02-09-wearetech-benin-2031-digital-strategy-roadmap|2026-02-15 Digital - Benin outlines its strategic vision for 2031
note: drafting opened 5-6 February 2026 with external facilitation, building on more than 3,000 km of fibre, the population register and more than 250 digital services

subject: gov.policy
name: Vision Bénin 2060 digital pillar
position_end: Digital pillar published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Authorisation of online media by the audiovisual regulator
milestone: Conventions signed with 89 online media outlets, 2026-10-01
position_end: The audiovisual and communication regulator signed conventions with 89 online radio, television and press outlets on 1 October 2026, closing its authorisation process for websites providing audiovisual and written-press services; the outlets now operate under the information and communication code and the digital code
note: the number of applicants refused is not stated

subject: gov.legislate
name: Banking and payments regulation statute
position_end: Payment and electronic-money institutions subject to licensing, permitted operations and supervision; the regional instant-payment instruction applies alongside it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Data-localisation law
position_end: Committed only; no draft, scope or timetable on file
note: committed in the presidential programme; no draft, scope or timetable is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital Code Article 550 on harassment through electronic communications
milestone: No amendment on file after the 2023 Universal Periodic Review recommendations
position_end: In force and used to prosecute journalists over social-media posts; a parliamentary workshop weighed amending it in November 2024, and the press-freedom body CPJ asked the new president in September 2026 to stop its use against the press

subject: gov.legislate
name: Décret 2020-209 instituting the exchange
position_end: In force; the signed decree now on file
note: the founding instrument of the national exchange, acquired 2026-08-04 from the operator's own media host; it is the signed decree rather than a Journal Officiel copy, and the PDF is a page-image scan with no text layer, so its articles cannot be quoted

subject: gov.legislate
name: Extension of the biometric register to foreigners and Afro-descendants
position_end: Residents file with distinct foreigner and Afro-descendant identifiers
note: law 2025-12 creates a residents file with distinct foreigner and Afro-descendant identifiers, for migration control and civic inclusion

subject: gov.legislate
name: Identification law of 2017
position_end: The statutory base for the identification of natural persons, creating the identification agency and the unique personal identifier
note: held as the OCR layer of a scan, so quotation from it is unsafe

subject: gov.legislate
name: Identity-linked SIM registration
position_end: In force
sources: 2025-02-22 Benin - unregistered SIM cards to be deactivated from 30 April 2025
note: the regulator ordered unregistered SIMs deactivated from 30 April 2025, an anti-fraud measure reporting noted itself demands a strong data-protection frame

subject: gov.legislate
name: Loi 2015-07 portant Code de l'information et de la communication
position_end: In force as the media and communication code, alongside the later digital code

subject: gov.legislate
name: Loi 2017-20 portant Code du numerique
milestone: Article 379 read against employer monitoring of work messaging
position_end: In force as the framework statute for the digital sector, adopted by the National Assembly on 13 June 2017, brought into conformity with the Constitution after two Constitutional Court decisions, promulgated on 20 April 2018 and since amended by Loi 2020-35. Every subsequent decree and regulator decision in this ledger cites it. Its reach into the workplace was set out in September 2026: on the newspaper’s reading of article 379, a company phone, a company-issued number or a work messaging group does not by itself entitle an employer to read the messages on it (2026-09)
note: the article 379 reading is a newspaper’s, not a regulator decision or a judgment; the repository holds no enforcement action on workplace monitoring

subject: gov.legislate
name: Tax measures pushing merchants onto digital rails
milestone: 1% levy on large cash payments, from 2025-01
position_end: Levy plus the 2026 rectifying finance law's digital taxes
note: a 1% levy on large cash payments and the 2026 rectifying finance law's digital taxes

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection authority
milestone: 907 files examined, 14 major litigation cases (2025 report)
position_end: 907 files, 64 control missions, 14 major litigation cases; no algorithmic-audit tooling or budget
note: created by the Code du numérique; its 2025 report records 907 files examined with 87.4% validated, 782 contentious, 64 control missions, 75 conformity certificates, 37 data-protection officers and 14 major cases examined in litigation; it flags its own gaps as the absence of algorithmic-audit tooling and budget

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection authority sworn officers
position_end: Seventeen officers of the data protection authority — four executives, eight trainees and five drivers — were sworn in before the Cotonou court of first instance on 14 September 2026 under article 468 of the digital code, formally binding them to the obligations of their duties
note: staffing, not enforcement: no case, sanction or inspection figure accompanies it

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection authority activity reporting
position_end: One activity report covering 2015 to 2020, published under article 481 of the 2018 digital code, with no later report on file
note: the duty is statutory and the repository holds nothing after 2020

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection authority authorisations of processing and transfer
position_end: The authority authorises processing and cross-border transfers case by case by published deliberation; the 2021 list of nine includes transfers to France, Morocco, Canada, Germany and Kenya
note: the published register runs to 2021; no later deliberations list is held

subject: gov.protect
name: Décret 2020-187 on police collection of travellers' data at borders
position_end: Authorises the Police républicaine to collect and process travellers' identity data and fingerprints at the borders, kept without a time limit and linkable to Interpol

subject: gov.protect
name: Décret 2022-107 on video-protection systems
position_end: Authorises data collection by video-protection systems run from a national command centre under the interior ministry, covering number plates, images and geolocation, with retention capped at 60 days

subject: gov.protect
name: Décret 2024-877 on police, judicial and prison information processing
position_end: A decree of 11 April 2024 sets how police, judicial and prison information is processed: ten criminal-justice files including DNA and biometrics, retention of 10 and 30 years, no right to object, and appeal to the data protection authority

subject: gov.protect
name: Enforcement against the electoral agency
position_end: Extraneous fields required to be stripped from the electoral roll before publication
sources: 2026-05-16 World Bank, African DPAs outline formula for trusted digital identity, DPI
note: the authority required extraneous fields to be stripped from the electoral roll before publication — a transparency-against-privacy question resolved by the regulator rather than the legislature

subject: gov.protect
name: Police and customs body-worn cameras
position_start: Authorised but not in routine use
position_end: Standard kit for traffic police in the largest city, on 500 devices and a dedicated information system authorised by the Council of Ministers and piloted from 2024 in three cities; who may view footage, how long it is kept and whether a citizen can obtain their own sequence remain unstated

subject: gov.regional
name: 50-in-5 digital public infrastructure campaign membership
position_end: 16th African member
note: 16th African member

subject: gov.regional
name: Cooperation agreement between the Beninese and Togolese data-protection authorities
position_end: The two authorities held a joint working session at Lome on 2 and 3 October 2026 on sharing experience and building skills, following the Togolese authority's mission to Cotonou on 18 August; the agreement's date and text are not held

subject: gov.regional
name: Cotonou Declaration on a single digital market
position_end: Ministerial commitments to 90% affordable broadband by 2030 and interoperable identity and payments
note: West and Central African ministers committed to 90% affordable broadband by 2030, interoperable identity and payments, doubled intra-African e-commerce, harmonised cyber, data and AI frameworks and 20m people with basic digital skills

subject: gov.regional
name: Data-protection cooperation conventions
position_end: Conventions with Senegal and Mali
note: with Senegal and Mali; the authority's president is vice-president of the francophone association and sits on the African network's executive committee

subject: gov.regional
name: ECOWAS-standard biometric identity card
position_end: In issue

subject: gov.regional
name: Free roaming with Senegal and Togo
position_end: Free roaming with Senegal and Togo, free incoming calls for 30 days
note: community free roaming under ECOWAS regulation C/REG.21/12/17, with free incoming calls for 30 days

subject: gov.regional
name: Participation in regional cybercrime enforcement
position_end: Participant in the regional takedown
note: among the states in the Carton Rouge 2.0 takedown, 651 arrests

subject: gov.regional
name: Six-country francophone AI-governance framework
milestone: Taken to the UN Global AI Dialogue 2026-07-09
position_end: Six-country governance guidelines adopted
note: adopted with five other francophone states and submitted to the UN Global AI Dialogue

subject: gov.regional
name: Smart Africa cross-border data exchange
milestone: Phase 1 completed on synthetic data; first controlled operational pilot targeted for early 2027, 2026-10-22
position_start: Cross-border digital identity pilot running with Rwanda and Ghana (2026-08)
position_end: Benin, Ghana and Rwanda have connected their national identity systems through the exchange and are moving towards real-world testing of mutual ID-card verification, planned for Benin-Rwanda air travel and Ghana-Benin land crossings. Smart Africa reported on 20 October 2026 that Phase 1 was complete, with the three national systems connected and identities verified end to end on synthetic data; Phase 2 prepares a controlled operational pilot for border identity checks, subject to national approvals and security assessments, which Smart Africa's transformation director said on 21 October 2026 is targeted for early 2027
sources: 2026-10-22-rwa-rwanda-ghana-benin-test-cross-border-digital-identity-verification|2026-10-20-xwa-benin-ghana-and-rwanda-take-major-step-towards-africas-single-digital|2026-10-19-xaf-biometricupdate-sadx-ben-gha-rwa-id-interop-live-testing|2026-08-11-giz-smart-africa-digital-sovereignty-interview|2026-04-27 Smart Africa drives cross-border data interoperability through SADX Technical Mission
note: with Rwanda and Ghana, working through PKI trust chains, API contracts, cross-border verification-request processing and incident response

subject: gov.regional
name: Trilateral border-modernisation steering committee
milestone: Joint Communiqué adopted 2026-07-27, establishing a Trilateral Strategic Steering Committee
position_end: Nigeria, Cameroon and Benin customs administrations committed to implement Beitbridge-model border modernisation on the Sèmè-Kraké and Mfum-Ekok corridors; at a joint assessment of the Seme-Krake post on 11 September 2026 Nigeria's customs offered real-time exchange of declarations, manifests, transit data, risk profiles and enforcement alerts, the two administrations sharing one post but no system
note: signed after a benchmarking mission to Beitbridge and Chirundu border posts; Bergmans Security Consultant and Supplies Limited and Bsmart Technologies sat on the benchmarking technical team alongside the three customs administrations

subject: gov.regional
name: UEMOA land registration harmonisation directive
milestone: Draft approved by eight member states, June 2026
position_start: No regional rule on land registration (2025-08)
position_end: Eight member states approved a draft directive harmonising land registration and titling rules across the union in June 2026, covering the establishment of urban land information systems; no domestic transposition is recorded (2026-06)

subject: gov.standards
name: Agence Nationale de Normalisation (ANM) and the NB conformity mark
position_end: Created by Decret 2017-031, operating the national NB conformity mark from April 2026, publishing solar photovoltaic standards, and recorded as a full ISO member

subject: gov.standards
name: Cadre d'interopérabilité
position_end: In force; its governance clause reports to the President
note: binds public and private bodies providing a public service; four levels of challenge, five common infrastructure components and named standards, with a governance clause stating the coordinating structure should report directly to the President of the Republic — an explicit answer to the question of who outranks a ministry that declines to connect

subject: gov.standards
name: Decree 2025-363 on electronic archiving providers
position_end: Electronic-archiving providers must be qualified trust-service providers, for three renewable years; its annex sets technical requirements including AES-256 encryption, two-factor authentication and ISO 14641

subject: gov.standards
name: Generative-AI compliance regime for public agents
position_end: Census of users, a binding charter and no-training contract clauses; concedes the sovereignty risk remains
note: starts from an admission that public agents already use generative-AI tools on personal accounts outside any framework, and calls for a census of those users and migration to secured arrangements, a binding harmonised charter, provider contracts carrying clauses forbidding any use of administration data to train or optimise models, reversibility and a prohibition on transfer to extraterritorial jurisdictions — and concludes that residual risks to digital sovereignty and technological dependence remain

subject: gov.standards
name: GovTech Maturity Index standing
position_end: 2025 top performer, alongside Algeria, South Africa and Nigeria
note: ranked a 2025 GovTech Maturity Index top performer alongside Algeria, South Africa and Nigeria; a reference index, cited and not absorbed

subject: gov.standards
name: National cybersecurity référentiel for AI systems
milestone: Presented to the state's information-systems directors, 8 October 2026
position_end: A national cybersecurity reference framework for artificial-intelligence systems, presented by the state digital agency on 8 October 2026: four risk tiers from minimal to unacceptable with controls for each, an AI officer and an ethics committee in each administration, and traceability of system decisions; no adopting instrument or date of application is held

subject: gov.standards
name: National Root Certification Authority and trust services
position_end: National root authority and trust services operating

subject: gov.standards
name: National vulnerability report
position_end: 878 vulnerabilities over 2021-2024, 23% critical; institutional compliance 6% to 87%
note: the first such report, covering 2021-2024: 878 recorded vulnerabilities of which 23% critical, with the public service worst hit at 326 cases, 832 password leaks, and institutional compliance ranging 6% to 87% — a deliberate act of transparency that tempers the success narrative

subject: gov.standards
name: PASI and PDAIE interoperability referentials
position_end: Under consultation
note: architecture and application-integration referentials consulted on to end siloed platform-building

subject: gov.standards
name: Published conditions of access to the exchange
position_end: Exchange conventions and authority authorisation before first connection
note: registration in the interoperable-solutions catalogue, demonstrated data governance, compatible infrastructure, conventions naming data, purposes, responsibilities and security measures, and for a private body an adhesion convention plus data-protection authority authorisation before first connection — which makes the authority a step in the technical onboarding path rather than a post-hoc complaint channel

subject: gov.discourse
name: Internet freedom ranking
position_end: 4th in Africa on a 2026 internet-freedom assessment
note: ranked 4th in Africa on a 2026 internet-freedom assessment; a reference ranking, cited and not absorbed

subject: gov.discourse
name: Internet governance school
position_end: a school on internet governance held in Ouidah with human rights at the centre of its programme

subject: finance.budget
name: Annual performance reports required by the organic budget law

subject: finance.budget
name: Audited figures for any digital budget line

subject: finance.budget
name: Budget standing of the digital institutions
position_end: The data-protection authority carries its own line (488.3m to 738.3m FCFA); the digital and identity agencies carry none
note: the data-protection authority carries its own budget line across three volumes (488.3m, 638.3m then 738.3m FCFA), while the digital agency that runs the CSIRT, data centre and PKI has no visible line in any of them and is funded from inside the sector programme; the identity agency likewise carries no programme of its own, and the telecoms regulator never appears in the finance law at all, being own-source funded from fees that fell 26.9% between 2024 and 2025 (the institutional-standing reading is this wiki's own compilation across the three estimates volumes, not a published analysis)

subject: finance.budget
name: Execution of the national digital budget programme
position_end: Programme 111 Numérique at 0.62% of credits ordonnancé (2026-04-30), against 15.43% across all programmes
note: the first per-programme execution figures Benin has ever published show programme 111 Numérique at 0.62% of credits ordonnancé at 30 April 2026 against 15.43% across all programmes, and 1.32% on the domestically financed portion alone, the whole of the execution being domestic because the programme's 6.5bn FCFA external loan tranche had drawn nothing; the ministry's own pilotage programme ran at 20.12%, so this is programme-specific rather than ministry-wide

subject: finance.budget
name: Quarterly budget execution reports (RAPEX)
milestone: Latest instalment held covers to 31 March 2026
position_end: Published quarterly; the instalments to 30 June, 30 September and 31 December 2025 and to 31 March 2026 are held, the last an image-only scan with no text layer
note: the Direction générale du Budget publishes an execution report at each quarter-end under décret n° 2015-035 portant Code de transparence, with a simplified citizen version; the citizen version at 31 December 2024 reports by economic nature and by function only — 2,507,185.8m FCFA executed against 2,551,700m provided, a 98.3% realisation rate, of which investment 38.29%, transfers 21.35% and personnel 20.86% — and carries no per-programme breakdown, so it yields no executed figure for any digital programme; the report at 31 March 2025 is held as a page-image artefact whose OCR layer is too corrupt to quote; the report at 31 March 2026 carries no text layer at all

subject: finance.mou
name: Sorbonne–Sèmè City framework agreement
position_end: Five-year renewal covering AI training, joint research and a planned innovation-management master's

subject: finance.new
name: Canadian financing for the digital transformation of women-led businesses
milestone: Announced during a ministerial visit, 4-6 August 2026
position_end: CAD5m for the digital transformation of women-led businesses, one of seven projects in a package of about CAD17m for Benin and West Africa; no implementing partner, start date or duration is named
note: the other six lines of the package are outside the digital estate; the digital line names neither a recipient organisation nor a delivery mechanism, so nothing here can yet be followed to a system

subject: finance.new
name: Chinese concessional loan for broadband network densification
position_end: A framework agreement for a RMB 265m (about FCFA 22bn) Chinese concessional loan, signed on 14 September 2021, to build a 484.1 km fibre backbone across Mono, Zou, Collines and the north and a 204.8 km metropolitan fibre network serving more than ten towns; the loan agreement itself, disbursement and delivery are not on file

subject: finance.new
name: Digital Rural Transformation Project (World Bank P162599)
position_end: Approved in July 2019; the fifth restructuring cancels a further EUR 4.57 million and cuts component costs from US$42.2 million to US$37.2 million, with the development objective still rated satisfactory

subject: finance.new
name: Economic governance for service delivery programme
position_end: A World Bank programme-for-results running since financial year 2023, whose results areas reach the tax directorate, public payments and public financial management systems

subject: finance.new
name: MEF digitalisation support project (BOAD)
position_end: XOF 19.5bn (US$32.5m) BOAD loan modernising the finance ministry's data centre, La Poste du Benin's information system and the DGFD's SGIFD/SIRH systems, in implementation (2026-05)

subject: finance.new
name: Private digital investment mobilised
position_end: US$215m committed by one operator through 2026; a privately financed 10 MW solar plant with a data facility; a regional venture fund approved

subject: finance.new
name: WARDIP second-phase regional digital financing
position_end: US$137m for Benin, Liberia and Sierra Leone across three pillars, Benin's share a EUR 51.1m (US$60.0m equivalent) IDA credit
sources: 2026-03-11-world-bank-ben-2026-wardip-sop2-benin|2026-03-16 New $137M initiative to enable digital service access for millions in three ECOWAS nations
note: US$137m announced for Benin, Liberia and Sierra Leone — broadband for more than 5m people and digital public services for more than 5m more, on infrastructure, business-environment and cross-border pillars

subject: infra.connect
name: 5G networks
position_end: Two operators, after Moov Africa Bénin
note: Moov Africa Bénin became the second 5G operator after MTN, which launched in 2024

subject: infra.connect
name: Benin IX internet exchange point
position_end: Operating and tracked in the Internet Society's IXP register; the Benin chapter's June 2023 study set out what its redynamisation, modernisation and sustainability would require

subject: infra.connect
name: Fixed and mobile internet subscriptions
position_end: 55,199 fixed internet subscriptions at 30 June 2025, a 0.42 per cent penetration, up from 28,816 a year earlier, 40,185 of them fibre to the home and 1,013 satellite; 10,573,802 active mobile internet subscriptions, down from 12,361,382 at end-2024, 22 per cent held by women
note: subscriptions, not users

subject: infra.connect
name: International connectivity programme
position_end: The earlier regional connectivity project closed and a second, US$137m across three countries, was approved; no bandwidth figure for Benin is published
note: No gigabit-per-second capacity figure is stated in either record

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet access provider authorisation regime (arrete of 28 August 2020)
milestone: Arrete of 28 August 2020 set the conditions of authorisation
position_end: Internet access provision moved from licensing to authorisation under the digital code, granted commune by commune with fees varying by commune, no national coverage obligation on entry and applications made online to the regulator; about ten providers were active beside the wholesale state infrastructure company (2021-06)
note: the regulator's own account; no later count of authorised providers is held

subject: infra.connect
name: Lagos–Accra terrestrial fibre route through Benin and Togo
position_end: A terrestrial route from Lagos to Accra through Benin and Togo, built with the state infrastructure company SBIN after the March 2024 subsea cable failures, at 11ms latency

subject: infra.connect
name: Licensing regime for non-terrestrial network services
position_end: ARCEP Decision 2024-108 sets the conditions under which non-terrestrial network service providers may operate, made under the digital code — the regime Starlink's Beninese subscriptions run under

subject: infra.connect
name: Measured 3G and 4G data speed by operator
position_start: the repository carries no position at the start of the period
position_end: the regulator's weekly readings placing the state-linked operator ahead of the two international groups on 3G and 4G data speed

subject: infra.connect
name: National fibre backbone
position_end: More than 3,000 km underpinning the service estate
note: more than 3,000 km of fibre underpins the service estate, cited as a foundation of the 2031 strategy

subject: infra.connect
name: Roaming agreement with Burkina Faso
milestone: Signed by the two regulators at Ouagadougou 2026-10-23
position_end: Benin's regulator signed a bilateral roaming agreement with Burkina Faso's at Ouagadougou on 23 October 2026, one of three Burkina Faso signed that day; the WAEMU Commission called for implementation timetables and monitoring of live links, tariffs and quality
note: no tariff or live date is stated

subject: infra.connect
name: Weekly publication of mobile quality-of-service indicators
position_end: Published weekly by the regulator for the mobile operators (2026-08)
note: A weekly series; the repository holds one week of it, so no trend can be read.

subject: infra.store
name: Data-centre capacity in country
position_end: Several data centres, one of them Tier III, about 2 MW in all and under-used (2026-04)
note: a figure given by the digital agency's head of strategy and architecture to a trade publication, not a published inventory

subject: infra.store
name: Isocel Telecom data centre
position_end: A neutral data centre run by an internet service provider for its large-account customers, opened in 2015 and billed by the company as the country's first
note: the company's own account; no capacity, tier or later operating account is held

subject: infra.store
name: MTN Benin data centre service
position_end: An operator data-centre service launched on 2019-06-14 for start-ups and firms of all sizes, still offered in 2023 as server rental and hosting with power, security and maintenance carried by the operator
note: the operator's own pages; no capacity or tier is published

subject: infra.store
name: National data centre
milestone: In operation at Abomey-Calavi under SBIM (2026-03)
position_end: Operating; no capacity, tier or tenancy figure held
note: operated at Abomey-Calavi by the state-owned SBIM; no capacity, tier or tenancy figure is held

subject: infra.store
name: Off-site backup provision
position_end: Provided for in the appraisal of the second regional digital integration project; no operating off-site backup is recorded

subject: infra.store
name: Secondary national data centre
position_end: A technical, economic and legal feasibility study tendered under the regional digital integration project for a redundant second data centre, not necessarily sited in Benin, to be completed within six months
note: the existing national data centre at Abomey-Calavi spans 300 square metres

subject: infra.store
name: Sovereign cloud and national cyber authority
milestone: Urged by an expert roadmap to 2033 (2026-04)
position_end: Recommended only; neither exists
note: urged by an expert roadmap to 2033; neither exists

subject: infra.energy
name: Benin Electricity Access Scale-Up Project (P173749)
milestone: US$200m IDA Scale-Up Facility credit appraised, May 2021
position_start: Financing approved for on-grid rural electrification, running to 2026 (2025-08)
position_end: US$200m approved, of which US$183m for on-grid electrification reaching about 150,000 rural households, running to 2026
note: An energy operation, held here because grid reach is what the digital estate outside the cities runs on.

subject: infra.energy
name: Grid reliability indices
position_end: Cotonou 2025: SAIDI 12.78, SAIFI 3.35; a 50 MW / 160 MWh storage order placed to smooth solar output, for completion in September 2027

subject: infra.capacity
name: PRSCG government systems capacity building
position_end: Nearly 100 ministerial IT staff trained to run the national network and data centre; a further training school opened in Cotonou

subject: infra.cybersec
name: AFIS fingerprint system wired to the regional police exchange
position_end: Connected to the ECOWAS SIPAO police data exchange
note: inaugurated 30 September 2025 and connected to the ECOWAS SIPAO police data exchange, EU-funded and Interpol-implemented

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Attack surface of the online service estate
position_end: More than 230 public services dematerialised, about 40 priority structures in close security cooperation (2025-07)
note: more than 230 dematerialised public services are described by the agency as leaving more of the state open to attack, with about 40 priority public and private structures in close security cooperation (July 2025); an expert roadmap to 2033 urges a sovereign cloud, a national cyber authority, a universal digital identity and AI-based intelligence fusion

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Club of information-security officers (Club des RSSI)
milestone: Constituted at its founding general assembly, 2026-09-26
position_end: An association of information-security officers across public and private institutions, constituted on 26 September 2026 with statutes adopted and an 11-member board, to pool expertise, train members, share lessons from security incidents in confidence and promote international standards; the head of cybersecurity at the national digital agency attended
note: a professional association rather than a state body; no membership count or work programme is published

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Decret 2021-550 approving the state information systems security policy
position_end: In force as the approved rules of the Politique de Securite des Systemes d'Information de l'Etat, made under the digital code

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National digital investigations centre complaint points
milestone: Three points opened at Porto-Novo, Abomey and Parakou, reported 2026-10-03
position_end: Complaints on personal-data breaches and digital offences are received at three points in police premises outside Cotonou, beside the Cotonou office and an email route

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National digital-security stack
milestone: CSIRT, PKI, forensic laboratory and critical-infrastructure policy in place
position_end: Committed to implementing the Malabo and Budapest conventions
note: a national digital-security strategy since 2020 with a national CSIRT, a national PKI, a forensic-analysis laboratory and a critical-infrastructure protection policy, with a stated commitment to implementing the Malabo and Budapest conventions

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Ransomware threats detected
position_end: 631 ransomware threats detected in Benin in 2024, on a security vendor's telemetry cited by Interpol
note: a detection count from one vendor's installed base, reported through Interpol's 2025 Africa assessment and repeated in a national newspaper interview, so the denominator - how much of Benin's estate that vendor sees - is unpublished and the figure cannot be read as national exposure. Two years old at the point of its citation, and the repository holds no incident, ransom-payment or recovery figure against it

subject: dpi.exchange
name: BIC-UEMOA credit information bureau
position_end: Operating across all eight UEMOA states with 321 data providers, about 48 million contracts and more than 20 million active borrowers; at its first Cotonou data forum on 23 July 2026 the finance ministry framed data quality as the route to cutting credit-approval turnaround to 48 hours
note: the figures are the bureau operator's own and are union-wide, not Benin-specific; no Benin coverage, dispute or data-protection statement is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Customs system migration
milestone: Migration from ASYCUDA completed at every office, announced 2025-04-15
position_start: 44 of 49 offices migrated, with more than 30bn CFA collected (2025-02)
position_end: The national customs management system migrated from ASYCUDA to the vendor's platform at every seaport, airport and land border office in fourteen months, with more than 100,000 declarations, 200,000 payments and 100,000 vehicle passes processed, 800 active users and 95 organisations on it; it is to be integrated with the single window, the port community system and electronic cargo tracking
note: the vendor's own release

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Customs systems interconnection at Seme-Krake
milestone: Nigerian customs in talks with a regional trade bank on the corridor, 2026-10-18
position_end: The two countries' customs administrations launched a pilot interconnection of their systems at the Seme-Krake border post on 11 September 2026, their directors-general presiding, to exchange data in real time and cut repeated formalities. No completion date or volume of declarations exchanged is published. Customs opened talks with a regional trade bank in Cairo on modernising the Seme-Krake and Mfum-Ekok corridors, including a declaration exchange system on a common data model; no cost or lending commitment was set (2026-10-18)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Electronic international waybill
position_end: Live at the Port of Cotonou
note: launched at the Port of Cotonou, mandatory after a three-month transition

subject: dpi.exchange
name: SECUROUTE road-enforcement data platform
milestone: Treasury directs road users to settle penalties through the portal by 2026-10-01
position_end: A public portal, securoute.anatt.bj, lets road users check unpaid traffic-offence penalties; the Treasury's communiqué of 2 September 2026 set 1 October 2026 for settlement, with forced recovery on the road after it, while the platform is extended for full interoperability with the national exchange
sources: 2026-09-11-ben-cadreco-tresor-penalites-routieres-paiement|2026-01-27 Cybastion Advances Digital Government Solutions, Supports Benin's SECUROUTE Infrastructure Upgrade
note: centralises and secures traffic and road-enforcement data across police, transport and road-safety agencies, being extended for full interoperability with the national exchange

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Single window for foreign trade (GUCE)
position_start: No position held at the window's opening
position_end: Operating since 2018 as the single platform for import, export and transit procedures, connecting the administrations involved, built by the vendor that later replaced the customs system; its e-payment module had recorded more than CFAF 900bn in electronic payments when the vendor handed the window to the government in July 2023
note: figures are the customs directorate's

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Socioeconomic impact measurement of digital public infrastructure
position_end: A pilot measuring the socioeconomic impacts of digital public infrastructure, with results and a stated way forward
note: a method pilot rather than a national measurement; no country-specific finding for this place is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Xroad-BJ national data exchange
position_end: 73 members, 176 information systems, 512 services; 138.17m requests cumulatively
note: instituted by décret 2020-209 and running on an X-Road-lineage platform; 138,174,337 total requests with 32.7m in the last 30 days, 73 members, 176 information systems and 512 services, the heaviest providers being land transport, identity and tax

subject: dpi.id
name: Biometric proof of life for pensioners
position_end: Pensioners prove they are alive from a smartphone: identification by personal identification number and pension booklet number, a fingerprint check in a dedicated application and confirmation by text message or email, with biometric kiosks in some public spaces as the alternative; the government announced the launch of the app for retirees of the national pensions fund on 15 October 2026, with a verification campaign running to 15 November 2026 and open to retirees living abroad; 15,189 proofs of life had been completed through the app by 21 October 2026
note: the 15,189 count is attributed by the outlet to sources close to the presidency, not to the ministry or the pensions fund

subject: dpi.id
name: Business intelligence environment over the national identity base
position_end: a tender opened by the identification agency for the architecture of a business-intelligence environment over its national identity data

subject: dpi.id
name: Citizen mobile wallet
position_end: Still planned; no build reported
sources: 2025-06-18 Benin envisages mobile wallet launch in inclusive national digital ID push
note: planned by end-2026, against a target of legal identity for every citizen by 2028

subject: dpi.id
name: Diaspora biometric passport renewal platform
position_end: Available in more than 80 countries, renewals reported at about 15 minutes
sources: 2025-10-24 Benin unveils platform to ease biometric passport applications for diaspora citizens|2025-12-18 Seamfix revealed as developer of Benin's biometric passport renewal app
note: available in more than 80 countries with renewals reported at about 15 minutes, built by an external vendor on the national exchange and tied to national identity and immigration systems

subject: dpi.id
name: Décret 2020-099 on the personal identification number
position_end: Makes the personal identification number mandatory for access to every public service and for data exchange between public and parapublic services; private bodies may use it for staff management or a service the holder asked for, but not as a search key or database key

subject: dpi.id
name: Foundational biometric identity
movement: Advanced, in issuance rather than in coverage
position_end: 98-99% biometric enrolment; 7.7m numbers and 6.1m certificates issued free
sources: 2026-05-20 Transforming lives in Benin a unique identification system|2024-06-27 WURI digital ID project improving access to public services in Benin|2025-11-01 Identification System in Benin Increasing Access to Services
note: the 2017 Identification Law created the agency and a unique personal identifier reaching about 10m in six months; the World Bank-supported programme added 2.2m more, lifting biometric enrolment to about 98-99%, with 7.7m personal identification numbers issued through the free lifelong card and 6.1m certificates issued free

subject: dpi.id
name: Identity record updates at arrondissement offices
milestone: Tablets issued to arrondissement secretaries from 2026-10-19
position_end: The identification agency began equipping arrondissement secretaries in several communes with tablets on 19 October 2026, so that users can update the signature and telephone number on their record locally rather than at the agency's main offices, alongside its mobile application and web portal; no count of communes or arrondissements is given

subject: dpi.id
name: Online renewal of the biometric national identity card
milestone: Opened to all on International Identity Day, 2026-09-16
position_end: Holders due for renewal can now start it through the identification agency's e-services platform, available at any hour, though the procedure is not fully automatic; no uptake figure

subject: dpi.id
name: Sustainability model for the digital identity system
milestone: International expert sought to define the model
position_end: An international expert sought to define a durable model for the identity system as the digital public infrastructure is built out (2026-09)
note: Identification is named as one of the pillars of the build; how it is to be paid for over time is the open question.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cashless motorway tolls
position_end: Cashless tolling live

subject: dpi.pay
name: GBESSOKE productive social safety net
position_end: 20,621 beneficiaries, 85% of them women, paid a first monthly instalment of 208,272,100 FCFA across twelve pilot communes onto free secured SIM cards, ahead of an intended extension to all 77 communes
note: eligibility was certified house by house by the statistics institute and the social affairs ministry

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mandatory electronic payment of court and chancellery fees
milestone: Fees for 109 acts fixed by interministerial arrêté, reported 2026-10-16
position_start: Fees paid in cash and by tax stamp under a 2012 decree
position_end: Decree 2026-617 of 18 September 2026 makes electronic payment the only way to pay fees for acts issued by the courts and the justice chancellery, stamps included, routes receipts to a dedicated Treasury account and repeals the 2012 decree; an interministerial arrêté fixes fees for 109 acts, a criminal-record extract at FCFA 1,900

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile money
position_end: 11.65m active accounts; one operator holds about 51% of accounts and 83% of revenue
note: 88.09% penetration on 11.65m active accounts at end-2025, one operator holding about 51% of accounts and about 83% of revenue, against 248.7m electronic-money accounts across the union in 2024

subject: dpi.pay
name: Regional central bank digital currency
position_end: The regional e-CFA in pilot
note: the regional e-CFA is in pilot, alongside a domestic debate on crypto-asset opportunity and risk

subject: dpi.pay
name: Regional instant payment rail
position_start: Rail launched across all eight member states (2025-09-30)
position_end: Fully interconnected and free domestically
note: the regional rail launched 30 September 2025 across all eight member states and free domestically; banks and mobile money were 100% interconnected by May 2026

subject: dpi.pay
name: SEMO official-missions system and electronic payment of mission expenses
status: Implemented, second phase instituted by circular
milestone: Proof of mission moved onto the SEMO+ mobile application, announced 2026-10-03
position_start: First phase (SEMO 1) in use for issuing, tracking and controlling official missions
position_end: The finance ministry's circular of 25 September 2026 institutes electronic payment of in-country mission expenses across all public administrations through the second phase of the official-missions system (SEMO 2); the first phase, run by the national control directorate, is credited with preventing overlapping missions and detecting fictitious agents, and geolocated proof of mission is to follow; proof of mission is now given on the SEMO+ mobile application, where the agent identifies by personal identification number, shares a location and validates by fingerprint, with fixed biometric kiosks as the alternative
note: no count of payments, agents or savings is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Tax e-services for small-business tax centres outside Cotonou
milestone: Parakou from 2026-09-21, Comè from 2026-09-28, Lokossa from 2026-10-05
position_end: The tax directorate is opening its online declaration and payment platform to taxpayers of the small-business tax centres at Parakou, Comè and Lokossa in stages from 21 September to 5 October 2026

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration
movement: Advanced, in the pilot but not in generalisation
position_end: Pilot at 76.56%; generalisation slipped 3 to 4 months into consolidation; a free campaign from 16 to 30 September 2026 issued a first birth certificate to 50,109 children under 14, on the identification agency's count
note: behind near-universal biometric coverage sits a weak civil-registration leg — about 2.5m births declared between 2021 and 2025 against under 1m actually registered, because parents had to make a second trip; a single-window pilot at 10 maternities lifted registration to 76.56% against about 22% nationally in 2025, and generalisation slipped 3 to 4 months into a consolidation phase

subject: dpi.registry
name: Business registration platform
milestone: Case-studied by the ILO as at 2021
position_end: monentreprise.bj registers economic units online, reachable from desktop and mobile, as the formalisation route for the informal sector
note: the case study carries no registration total

subject: dpi.registry
name: Death registration
milestone: Catch-up registration of deaths since November 2017 opened 2025-10-31
position_end: Deaths are declared to the neighbourhood or village chief of the place of death and certificates issued free at identification-agency units in town halls; a catch-up operation registered deaths undeclared between 1 November 2017 and 6 November 2025 to update the population register, and declaration must now precede any funeral under article 31 of loi 2020-34
note: no count of deaths registered by the operation is held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Decret 2025-679 on registration of children under 14
milestone: Cited in September 2026 as permitting registration on the prosecutor's requisition
position_end: Permits, under certain conditions, the registration of children under 14 on the requisition of the public prosecutor and on witness testimony, for children without a legal identity
note: known from a press account; the decree's text and date are not held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Décret 2023-491 creating the Registre social unique, amended by Décret 2024-978
position_end: Created by decree on 26 September 2023 and amended in June 2024 to take in households exposed to shocks, notably climatic ones; its June 2024 procedure manual requires the identification number to enrol and shares beneficiary lists over the national data exchange, with more than 300,000 households held
note: both decrees are held as scans with no text layer; their content is read from the catalogue record

subject: dpi.registry
name: e-Foncier national land cadastre
milestone: First commune with complete cadastral coverage
position_end: Parakou became the first commune with complete cadastral coverage, 196,474 parcels registered across about 56,390 hectares, presented at the town hall on 1 September 2026 to a Netherlands embassy delegation. The platform's data put 38 per cent of registered parcels in men's ownership against 7 per cent women's and 3 per cent collectivites, with the owners of 21 per cent unidentifiable, 24 per cent of parcels not recasees, 7 per cent domaines and no parcel recorded as contested; more than 11,500 cadastral registration certificates had been distributed door to door by that date. Municipal officials named the next steps as continued data updating and certificate distribution, formalising land transactions through the platform, making the 2025 cadastre decree operational, and adding platform functions for recasement attestations, mutation certificates and compulsions
note: the ownership breakdown is the useful half: a fifth of registered parcels have an owner the register cannot identify, and women hold a seventh of what men hold on the platform's own count

subject: dpi.registry
name: Identifiant Fiscal Unique (Decret 2017-215)
position_end: In force as the single fiscal identifier, alongside the SIGTAS tax system deployed from March 2018

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Register of Natural Persons
position_end: More than 13.8m people registered (2026-05); 80+ institutions, about 200,000 authentications a day, 25m eKYC verifications in 2025
sources: 2026-05-01-ben-anip-id4africa-2026-gestion-integree-crvs-id|2026-02-02 Benin reports 75% of identification services accessed through digital platforms|2026-01-28 Benin Advances E-Government With Mass Digital ID Adoption
note: connects more than 80 institutions at about 200,000 biometric authentications a day; in 2025 at least 75% of identification services went digital, across 10.5m services and 25m electronic know-your-customer verifications

subject: dpi.registry
name: National street and door addressing strategy
position_end: A harmonised national addressing strategy is in preparation: the Council of Ministers took it up in April 2026 and the environment and transport ministry convened the sector's actors on 21 May 2026. No adopted strategy, coverage figure or address count is held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Population register as the electoral roll
milestone: Used for the presidential poll of 2026-04-12
position_start: Statutory basis in place, untested at a presidential poll
position_end: Compiled and managed the April 2026 list; ECOWAS and AU missions satisfied
sources: 2025-08-02 Benin - ANIP unveils digital platforms to modernise the electoral process|2026-04-11-techreviewafrica-ecowas-au-benin-electoral-roll|2026-04-08-anip-voter-identification-scrutin
note: the register is the single source of electoral data under law 2017-08; the agency compiled and managed the list for the 12 April 2026 presidential poll, ECOWAS and African Union missions assessed its preparedness and pronounced themselves satisfied, and card fees were waived with web, mobile, USSD and photo-update channels open to polling morning

subject: dpi.registry
name: Registre Social Unique
milestone: Created in Conseil des ministres, January 2026
position_end: An information system registering households and deciding eligibility across social-protection programmes, classifying them as non-poor, non-extreme poor and extreme poor and updated periodically, so that cash and in-kind transfers, health insurance, training, credit and pension schemes draw on one secured socio-economic database
note: the two social-protection programmes already running are named among its users; the 2023 creation decree and its 2024 amendment are held as their own row

subject: dpi.registry
name: TERRA land governance programme
position_end: A national land programme with a finalised operations manual, run by the land agency under the ministry of economy and finance with World Bank support
note: it sits alongside the cadastre platform rather than replacing it

subject: dpi.mis
name: AI, drone and geospatial malaria programme
position_end: Incidence down 38% and mortality down 39% across 2022-2024
note: US$2.3m with Japanese financing; incidence down 38% and mortality down 39% across 2022-2024

subject: dpi.mis
name: AlafiaComm community health app
position_end: A donor-funded mobile app for community health relays, built to be interoperable with DHIS2 and the national health information system, in pilot
note: the 2021 account is the latest held; no scale-up is on record

subject: dpi.mis
name: Commercial court of Cotonou e-services platform
milestone: Three further e-services made online-only from 2026-02-16
position_start: No position held at the window's opening
position_end: Online filing and fee payment for the commercial court, opened to lawyers and bailiffs in March 2021 with public case tracking; by order of 12 February 2026 applications and fees for ex parte petitions, opposition to payment orders and the executory formula became online-only from 16 February 2026, with copies of judgments to follow from 1 March
note: one court; the 2026 volumes cited are the court's own (1,095 ex parte petitions in 2025)

subject: dpi.mis
name: Demographic dividend monitoring platform
position_start: Not previously held by this repository
position_end: The country is taking part with seven other West African states in the pilot phase of a platform to monitor progress on the demographic dividend, at a regional meeting in Abidjan from 7 to 9 September 2026 whose sessions test and improve the tool before wider deployment.
note: no indicator set, data source, host institution, funding or deployment date for the platform is published, and what the country contributes to it is not stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Digital platform for identifying and geolocating producers and plots
milestone: Approved within an agricultural productivity package
position_end: The Council of Ministers approved an agricultural productivity package including a digital platform for identifying and geolocating producers and plots and for tracking inputs and yields
note: one line of a cabinet record: no design, operator, budget, coverage or relationship to the existing land cadastre is stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: E-justice information system and court interconnection project
milestone: Technical feasibility study due to start October 2024
position_start: No position held at the window's opening
position_end: Framed at a scoping workshop in April 2022 as a global information system for criminal and civil procedure over a private network linking 110 justice sites, courts, appeal courts, police stations and prisons; a feasibility study for the network was due to begin in October 2024, with a consultancy to be appointed by September
note: a news report citing a local source; the 2026-2033 justice digitalisation plan is held as its own row

subject: dpi.mis
name: Educmaster school management system
position_end: The national education management information system covers nursery through secondary, technical and vocational, and its portal reports 1,804,826 learners, 63,305 teachers and 17,330 schools
note: the order records that many schools had used it only for final-year examination entries

subject: dpi.mis
name: Health management information system
milestone: Private facilities brought into reporting from 2023
position_end: DHIS2 carries ministry reporting, with private health facilities trained from 2023 to submit reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health data that had gone largely unreported
note: 752 private facilities sat outside the reporting chain before the training

subject: dpi.mis
name: Health-facility geo-registry and master facility list
milestone: Link to the national health information system left unfinished
position_end: A geo-registry built on the IASO platform consolidates the master list of health facilities; the automatic feed into the national DHIS2 was left unfinished when the project ended
note: the account is the platform vendor's own

subject: dpi.mis
name: Online laisser-passer for foreign vehicles
position_end: Customs issues laisser-passer for foreign vehicles wholly online through the national platforms
note: announced by customs; no volume, fee or processing time is given

subject: dpi.mis
name: Payroll-procedure decree run through the integrated HR and payroll system (SIGRHP)
status: Enacted, adopted in Council of Ministers 2026-03-04
position_end: A decree adopted on 4 March 2026 ends payment of salaries without prior authorisation and puts the whole pay chain through the integrated HR and payroll system SIGRHP

subject: dpi.mis
name: Tax directorate information system modernisation
milestone: Project fiche republished 2026-08-20; project runs to 2026-12-31
position_end: A EUR 2m donor-funded project for the digital transformation of the tax directorate's information systems, running from 9 August 2023 to 31 December 2026
note: a project fiche rather than a progress report; no delivery, module or completion status is published four months before the stated end date. the tax directorate's own strategic orientation plan for 2023-2027 is the instrument behind the work, and the repository had held it only from the financing side

subject: dpi.govtech
name: ACTIA academic records platform (Universite d'Abomey-Calavi)
milestone: Made the sole channel by rectorate note of 31 July 2026
position_end: Mandatory for all requests for degree certificates, transcripts, enrolment certificates and diploma duplicates at UAC; no fee schedule, turnaround time or appeal route published
note: One university's platform, not a national service.

subject: dpi.govtech
name: e-Procurement platform
milestone: Regulator's 2025 report: build tender halted, recruitment carried into 2026, March 2026
position_start: Old platform retired by décret 2025-169, new one not built, the first build tender declared unsuccessful (2025-09)
position_end: Procurement bodies were trained from 6 October to 28 November 2025 on the new legal framework, the regulator citing a 2024 evaluation in which only 21 of 757 calls published in 2023 reached the automatic contract stage on SIGMaP; on 19 December 2025 the treasury announced that SIGMaP and the procurement web portal are replaced by the new e-Procurement platform and presented its modules, alongside décret 2025-363 on electronic archiving providers. No go-live date or build contract award is stated. The regulator's activity report to 31 December 2025 states that the international tender launched on 13 June 2025 was declared unsuccessful and the procedure halted, that FCFA 1.2bn of payment credits for the platform went unspent in 2025, and that recruitment of an integrator continues in 2026
note: décret 2025-169 costed the new platform at 3.3bn FCFA on World Bank financing

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Integrated economic, social and digital centres
position_end: The Council of Ministers approved on 2 September 2026 the construction of 35 integrated economic, social and digital centres across 26 communes, each bringing a social protection single window, a postal agency and a community digital point together in one location
note: approved as a construction programme with no cost, timetable, service list or operating model published, and no statement of how the three functions in each centre are to work together

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Justice-sector digitalisation plan 2026-2033
position_end: Citizen case-tracking portal and secure hosting committed; no budget, sequencing or implementing agency
note: commits to a citizen portal for case tracking, secure public hosting of judicial, notarial and bailiff instruments, digitally integrated legal aid and an heir identification mechanism; the primary contains no e-greffe, no direct court-police-prison data link, no blockchain authentication and no judicial security operations centre, contrary to secondary accounts, and no budget, sequencing or implementing agency is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National Administrative Simplification Prize
milestone: Launched by communiqué 2026-10-12; submissions 29 October to 12 November 2026
position_end: A presidential prize inviting public servants, citizens and firms to propose simpler procedures, digitised procedures and data sharing between administrations among them, towards the stated goal of every procedure online by 2030

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Online loss certificates
position_start: Issued on paper at police stations
position_end: The national police issues loss certificates only through its documentation centre's online platform from 1 October 2026, with electronic payment, under a service note signed that day by the director general; police stations no longer issue the certificate and are to direct and assist people declaring a loss
note: no fee or volume is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Portail national des services publics
position_end: More than 230 public services dematerialised by July 2025; more than 250 digital public services cited in February 2026
note: more than 230 public services dematerialised, electronic payment included, by July 2025; more than 250 digital services are cited in the 2031 strategy material

subject: dpi.govtech
name: UnivServices.bj national university services platform
position_end: A national portal for students at four public universities, with transport the first live service and catering, housing and health announced to follow; no user count

subject: digital.localgov
name: Civil registry dematerialisation framework
position_end: The framework stands and the single-window pilot runs in ten health facilities

subject: digital.localgov
name: Commune revenue cash-desk software (PAACOL)
milestone: Deployed at single revenue windows in 12 communes, 2019-20
position_end: Networked cash-desk software logging every payment at single revenue windows in 12 communes under a communes-association project of 2019-20; the association's digital commission was still discussing the digitisation of commune revenue collection in June 2025, with connectivity named first; nothing later on the software's use is held

subject: digital.localgov
name: Döton citizen complaints app (Adjarra commune)
position_start: No position held at the window's opening
position_end: A mobile application through which residents of Adjarra report complaints about communal services and infrastructure, handled by a dedicated cell at the town hall with real-time tracking, available from 14 February 2025
note: one commune; no complaint count is published

subject: digital.localgov
name: e-Communes municipal services platform
position_end: Live and piloted in three communes of 77; one town hall equipped with solar power, network connectivity and an official municipal site

subject: digital.localgov
name: National administration network reach to town halls
milestone: 12 more town halls on the network's services in 2024
position_end: 187 authorities, ministries, the presidency and prefectures, were connected in one administrative network by May 2023, with every municipality to follow; the government's 2025 bond report counts 12 more town halls using the network's services in 2024; no total of town halls connected is held

subject: digital.rural
name: Digital classrooms in rural primary schools
position_end: Equipment placed from 2019 and a teacher-training campaign across 46 centres in six mostly rural northern departments
note: Teacher skills rather than pupil-facing equipment in the later record

subject: digital.rural
name: Police information systems outside the capital
position_end: Regional extension from 2019, the fingerprint system in service, and 300 officers including 150 arrondissement commissioners trained across six cities

subject: digital.rural
name: Rural health data capture
position_end: Aggregate reporting from every health zone on the national platform; a tablet-based household capture reaching the whole territory
note: Aggregate statistical reporting, not electronic records at each clinic

subject: tech.ai
name: African-language model track at the national AI meeting
position_end: The national edition of the continental machine-learning meeting opens a track on large language models, generative artificial intelligence and low-resource African language corpora, at Cotonou from 10 to 12 September 2026 (2026-09)
note: an event with a stated track; no corpus, participant number, output or funding is stated, and it had not yet taken place when this was written

subject: tech.ai
name: AI-assisted malaria diagnosis in referral hospitals
milestone: Health ministry contract awarded for 20 units, reported 2026-09-08
position_start: In use in individual health facilities, outside the national malaria programme
position_end: Twenty miLab MAL units are to be deployed in the main public referral hospitals under a health ministry contract with the South Korean firm Noul, with deployment to extend to further public facilities; the national malaria control programme has classified the device as a point-of-service diagnostic and recommended its use in malaria control. The device automates blood-smear preparation, digitisation and AI analysis of the images
note: the contract award date is unestablished; the account attributes the award to South Korean outlets that are not held. The supporting trial is the vendor's own reporting of a 2025 clinical evaluation in northern and southern university hospitals covering 211 children with suspected severe malaria, put at 98.82% sensitivity and 100% specificity against manual microscopy with examination time cut to under 20 minutes from about 75

subject: tech.ai
name: Data-protection authority AI policy
position_end: A dedicated AI policy with strict purpose limitation
sources: 2026-05-16 World Bank, African DPAs outline formula for trusted digital identity, DPI
note: a dedicated AI policy with strict purpose limitation, noted as one of the few African data-protection authorities to hold one

subject: tech.ai
name: Dedicated AI legislation
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-10 — a four-country comparative study found no AI-specific legislation in force or in draft
milestone: Digital agency called for AI-specific rules in its September 2026 bulletin; no instrument on record
position_end: None published; the digital agency's quarterly bulletin of September 2026 called for AI-specific rules on governance, liability and compliance beyond the digital code and the data-protection regime, proposing risk-tiered regulation and a national doctrine classifying systems as prohibited, subject to reinforced assessment or deployable under transparency and security duties; it names no legal vehicle, authority or timetable
note: the national AI and big-data strategy carries the field; the study rates Cote d'Ivoire's strategy the most advanced of the four on inclusion and data governance

subject: tech.ai
name: Digital code offence of manipulating a person's image (article 576)
milestone: Penalties restated by the digital investigations centre, 2026-05-29
position_start: In force under the digital code
position_end: The national digital investigations centre warned in October 2025 against AI-faked videos and on 29 May 2026 restated that altering, generating or spreading a person's image by AI without consent is punishable under article 576 of the digital code by up to five years and XOF 25m

subject: tech.ai
name: FFSTC Fongbe-French speech translation corpus
position_end: About 31 hours of Fongbe speech with French transcriptions, compiled at the mathematics and physical sciences institute at Dangbo, with baseline speech-translation models scoring BLEU 8.96 and 8.14
note: an academic resource; no use in a public service is on file

subject: tech.ai
name: GPT BJ government virtual assistant
milestone: Expansion of the assistant tendered by the digital agency, June 2024
position_end: Launched at the 2023 digital entrepreneurship and AI fair as a chatbot answering questions on the tax, digital, labour and penal codes; the digital agency tendered a conversational-assistant platform and new use cases in June 2024

subject: tech.ai
name: Identity agency virtual assistant
milestone: Feasibility study for a multilingual voice assistant awarded 2025-10-20
position_end: The identity agency ANIP presented its e-services portal and a mobile app with a virtual assistant in February 2025; in October 2025 a five-month feasibility study of a multilingual voice AI for online identity-document requests was awarded for XOF 47.7m under the World Bank identity project

subject: tech.ai
name: National AI and big-data strategy
position_end: the strategy in force, with an external policy assessment arguing that the country must convert its lead in artificial-intelligence governance into results
note: the 2023-2027 strategy; Benin rose from 145th globally to the sub-Saharan top five on an AI-readiness index in three years

subject: tech.ai
name: National-language voice data collection
milestone: 700 hours of Fongbe audio from 2,400 contributors
position_start: Not previously held by this repository
position_end: A national-language project has collected 700 hours of Fongbe audio from 2,400 contributors across more than 20 zones and localities in a few months, reported 8 September 2026, run by the state digital systems agency with an inclusive-digital institute to build training material for artificial intelligence in Beninese languages. The account raises what happens to the data once the voices are recorded.
note: no licence, consent basis, custody arrangement, release plan or model built on the corpus is published, which is the question the account itself puts

subject: tech.ai
name: State of AI Policy in Africa score
position_end: 13 of 24 on a twelve-criterion rubric of policy design and delivery, an early, costed strategy and inclusive participation against slow implementation and thin ethical and legal depth (October 2025)
note: a private analysts' index; earlier editions are not held

subject: tech.ai
name: Tax and customs data-science use cases (Data Governance in Africa)
position_end: A customs revenue dashboard consolidating the two customs systems with next-day updates, a mirror-trade analysis against partner declarations, and a model classifying standardised-invoice item labels for the tax directorate
note: the implementing consultancy's own account

subject: tech.ai
name: Technical advisers on artificial intelligence in ministries
milestone: Advisers appointed at several ministries, 2 September 2026
position_end: The Council of Ministers appointed technical advisers on artificial intelligence at several ministries, including at the digital transformation and innovation ministry, which the minutes describe as in charge of the national artificial intelligence strategy
note: the minutes are the repository's confirmation of which ministry holds the artificial-intelligence strategy; the strategy itself is not published and the advisers' remit is not stated

subject: tech.industry
name: Domestic content-verification platform
position_end: Checks text, images, audio and video, including AI-generated content
note: founded 2025, checking text, images, audio and video including AI-generated content

subject: tech.innovate
name: Decret 2023-095 on the start-up label
position_end: In force, setting how the start-up label is granted to micro, small and medium enterprises and the rights and obligations that come with it

subject: tech.innovate
name: Domestic payment aggregator
position_end: A home-grown rail with more than 13,000 merchants
note: more than 13,000 merchants on a home-grown rail — a rare Beninese-owned layer in a regionally supplied stack

subject: tech.innovate
name: Position in the continental startup scene
position_end: An assessment of the country's emerging position in the continental startup scene, running from the commercial capital to the interior
note: an outlet's assessment; no funding total, company count or comparative ranking is carried here

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Digital technology and educational inequality
position_end: An account of the governance trends around digital technology in education and the inequality they produced
note: a 2023 analysis rather than a programme; no enrolment, device or attainment figure is held, and nothing later reports whether the trends it names have changed

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Domestic AI authorship and frugal-AI argument
position_end: A strategy co-author's frugal-AI argument, published 2026-07
note: a co-author of the national AI strategy published a build-an-LLM-from-scratch book arguing for frugal domestic AI, with a GPU-scarcity route to AI becoming a luxury good as the sharpest claim

subject: capacity.literacy
name: SADA digital skills initiative
position_end: The initiative stands alongside a donor digital programme at mid-term evaluation and a civil-society inclusion effort; no population literacy rate is published

subject: capacity.training
name: Cotonou AI academy
position_end: A city-government track in artificial intelligence, robotics and digital fabrication for pupils of the city's public secondary schools, opened as a ten-day campus for a first cohort of 60 pupils and the first stage of a four-year programme
note: a municipal programme; no budget, curriculum or progression route beyond the first cohort is published

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital classrooms in general secondary schools
position_end: UNICEF handed the secondary education ministry 628 items of computer equipment for 43 schools in nine departments and eight departmental directorates, enough for 12 new digital classrooms alongside the 55 already deployed in its intervention areas
note: an in-kind donation whose value the government release does not state

subject: capacity.training
name: ICDL certification programme for public administration staff
milestone: Second wave of 351 officials planned for 2024
position_end: A nine-month ICDL training and certification programme launched on 2022-07-12 for 1,540 officials, 70 per ministry; about 1,500 trained in the first phase, with a second wave of 351 planned for 2024
note: no certification or pass count is published for either wave

subject: capacity.training
name: Institut de Formation et de Recherche en Informatique (IFRI)
milestone: Listed in the national university's 2023-2024 statistical yearbook
position_start: No position held at the window's opening
position_end: The national university's computing institute at Abomey-Calavi offers professional bachelor's and master's degrees in software engineering, internet and multimedia, computer security, and information systems and networks; the university enrolled 62,175 students in 2023-2024, down 4.1 per cent
note: the captured part of the yearbook carries no enrolment figure for the institute

subject: capacity.training
name: National AI Olympiad
position_end: First edition held

subject: capacity.training
name: National tele-teaching platform
position_end: Authorised, not built
note: authorised by the Council of Ministers across four public universities for 2026-27, with virtual amphitheatres for hinterland students

subject: capacity.training
name: State RSSI certification programme
position_end: About 85 officers trained (2026-08) against a target of 100 qualified RSSI by end-2026, on CEH and ISO 27001 with practical work at the national Cyber Range; intake opened beyond central government to local authorities, state enterprises and the private sector
note: the 85-trained and 100-by-end-2026 figures are the agency's own, given at the launch and not independently verified; the programme is framed as part of implementing the national digital-security strategy and the PSSIE

subject: capacity.training
name: Sèmè City skills hub network
milestone: Hub network with a Sorbonne partnership
position_end: Hub network plus a francophone digital-skills programme and an annual digital week
note: a hub network with a Sorbonne partnership and online hubs, alongside a francophone digital-skills programme and an annual digital week

subject: capacity.training
name: École des Métiers du Numérique
position_end: The school stands; two operator-run cohorts certified in the window, one of 60
note: No enrolment or graduation figure is published for the school itself

subject: capacity.research
name: National science and technology university
position_end: UNSTIM at Abomey trains in science, technology, engineering and mathematics across more than nine constituent entities
note: the captured page carries no date of its own

subject: capacity.research
name: University AI strategy and ethical framework
position_end: The national university adopted its own AI strategy, ethical framework and usage charter aligned to the national strategy; a research institute launched a national-language AI project

subject: include.access
